clue.text: US checks over Republican scams

indicators.note: over says the checks are placed around, covering, the Republican letter

parts.note: in American usage a tick mark is called a check

explanation.surface: American political commentary: some check marks over a Republican's schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricks and scams are both deceptions used to cheat someone, so the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Like Bacardi but could go after gin here

definitions.meaning: Bacardi is a brand of rum, so like it means rum-like
the card game played as gin plus this word, a variety where gin precedes it

explanation.surface: A rum-like drink that might follow gin at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the spirit but completes the card game name gin rummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: tasting of rum; noun sense: a card game whose variant is gin rummy.

clue.text: Mischief-maker chasing child's a little monkey

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the mischief-maker follows the abbreviation for child

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for child; the 's is just a link
an imp is a mischievous sprite or child

explanation.surface: A naughty kid running after a child is called a little monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A chimp is an ape; 'a little monkey' is loose, in the sense of a cheeky primate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees are primates casually lumped with monkeys, and the phrase also evokes a playful youngster.

clue.text: You and I objectively backing computer department proceedings

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the pronoun is reversed

parts.note: the objective case of 'you and I' is us
IT (information technology) is the computer department

explanation.surface: We two support legal action by the IT department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objectively' means the grammatical object case, not impartially.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal proceedings brought in court are a lawsuit, a case.

clue.text: VP adopts a note of forbearance

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the vice-president's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Mike Pence was US Vice-President under Trump
TI is a note of the sol-fa scale (te)

explanation.surface: A vice-president takes up a tone of tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: VP points to Mike Pence, US Vice-President 2017-21.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance is calm tolerance and restraint under provocation, which is what patience means.

clue.text: Midday about time to shore up river barge

indicators.note: in a down clue, to shore up is to sit beneath, so the river comes on top

parts.note: the Po is a river in northern Italy

indicators.note: about says the word for midday goes around the letter for time

parts.note: midday is noon

explanation.surface: A river barge propped up at noon.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue a support sits underneath, so 'to shore up' puts the river on top; 'barge' is a noun here, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed boat used to support a floating bridge is a kind of barge.

clue.text: Orchestrated tuba with E-minor instrument

indicators.note: orchestrating means arranging music, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A piece scored for tuba in E minor with another instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine is a percussion instrument, a hand-held drum with jingles.

clue.text: Tablet dropped by sailor at the French fair

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
to drop something is to quit it
AB (able seaman) is a sailor
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French sailor drops a tablet at a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'at' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of just and impartial is a synonym for treating everyone evenly.

clue.text: Dressmakers from court mess about

indicators.note: about means around in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seamstresses fooling about in the royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who make or supply theatrical clothes are dressmakers, so the agent nouns match.

clue.text: End morning piece working around one

indicators.note: around says the earlier pieces surround the letter for one

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning (ante meridiem)
a bit is a piece
a machine that is working is on
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone finishing a morning's work on a piece that revolves around a single thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' reads as a verb but is the noun definition; the I goes between AMBIT and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An end in the sense of an aim or goal is what you strive for, a synonym of the noun here.

clue.text: Articulate American beast that may make your hair stand on end

definitions.text: that may make your hair stand on end

indicators.note: articulate means spoken clearly, so the word for the beast is said out loud

parts.note: the moose is the North American name for the elk

explanation.surface: A hair-raising American animal that speaks clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair styling foam is applied to give volume and lift, literally helping hair stand up.

clue.text: State representative hot for young temptress

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York State
an MP (Member of Parliament) is an elected representative
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A state politician with a hot young seductress.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive young woman is called by the name of the mythical maidens of nature, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Individual entrées of salmon on Lyonnaise onions

indicators.note: an entrée is an entrance, so the entrances of these words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A single serving of salmon starters on onions cooked Lyonnaise style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrées' plays on the menu sense; here it means the starting letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done alone, by one person, is individual, so the adjective fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Rowdy Yank put in hospital

indicators.note: put in says the letter for hospital is placed inside the word for a pull

parts.note: to yank is to tug
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A rowdy American is admitted to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Yank is the verb 'pull', not an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy is a noisy violent ruffian, so the noun is a synonym for a violent hoodlum.

clue.text: Disorganised scout sales are hopeless affairs

indicators.note: something disorganised is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poorly run Scout fundraising sales are doomed ventures.
explanation.definitionFit: Causes that cannot succeed are hopeless undertakings, an idiom for doomed efforts.

clue.text: Awkward b. completely overturned objections at first

indicators.note: at first says the overturned objections come before the expanded abbreviation
overturned says the word for objections is turned the other way round

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'
b. is short for born, so written out completely it is the full word

explanation.surface: A clumsy note on someone's birth date overturning early objections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completely' asks for the abbreviation b. in full.
explanation.definitionFit: An awkward, difficult person is obstinate and uncooperative, a common sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Score individual number

parts.note: a score is twenty
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A tally of one person's results gives a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: It is also the card game vingt-et-un, in keeping with the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty plus one is simply a cardinal figure, a number.

clue.text: Disregard little oldie getting up wearing rollers perhaps

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the blinds hold the reversed abbreviation

parts.note: roller blinds are an example of blinds

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means rising, so the abbreviation reads upwards

parts.note: SEN, short for senior, is a little word for an old person

explanation.surface: An old lady ignoring things while getting up in hair rollers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rollers' suggests hair curlers but points to roller blinds; 'Disregard' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilful blindness, a refusal to see, is a figurative sense of ignoring something.

clue.text: Masseuse uses extracts of shrub berries

indicators.note: an extract is a piece drawn out, so the letters are taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A masseuse rubs in oils made from shrub berries.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rubs someone down is a masseur or masseuse, so the agent noun fits.

clue.text: Society divorcée takes on leading MCP

parts.note: a former spouse is an ex
first place, written 1st, is leading; the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A society divorcée takes on a prominent male chauvinist.
explanation.walkthrough: MCP is 'male chauvinist pig'; the 1 of 1ST is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A male chauvinist pig is a man prejudiced against women, the noun sense of the word for a gender bigot.

clue.text: European refusal to feel rubbish

parts.note: non is French for no
to sense is to feel

explanation.surface: A European rejecting the idea that feelings are rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish in the sense of foolish talk is a synonym for absurd drivel.

clue.text: Call from Democrat opposing the President?

definitions.meaning: in bridge a call is a bid, here one with no suit as trumps
a Democrat opposing President Trump might say no to Trump

explanation.surface: A rallying cry from a Democrat against the President.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a bid with no trump suit fits the card theme.
explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge a bid is a call, and this one names play with no trump suit.

clue.text: Detailed research into boss

indicators.note: de-tailed, its tail removed, so the last letter of the word for research goes

parts.note: a study is a piece of research

explanation.surface: An in-depth investigation into a manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as thorough but splits as de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or ornamental stud, as on a shield or ceiling.

clue.text: Bet Italian smoker lapses back

indicators.note: lapsing back means falling backwards, so the volcano's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Etna is a smoking volcano in Sicily, Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian smoker relapses, and someone places a bet on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake put up before cards are dealt in poker is a bet, a gambling sense.

clue.text: Loud drunkard is loaded

parts.note: F (forte) is the musical direction for loud
a lush is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A noisy drunk is loaded, i.e. plastered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' seems to mean drunk; it means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being loaded with money and being flush both mean having plenty of cash.

clue.text: Some popular variety of grub

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some popular kind of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'of grub' is changed to 'grub': 'of' is a link word, and a larva is a grub, not 'of grub'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the soft worm-like young stage of an insect, a synonym.

clue.text: Capture spies allegedly

indicators.note: allegedly means it is said so, which signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: to spy is to see, so spies means sees

explanation.surface: Spies are said to have been captured.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture is to take hold of forcibly, a direct synonym of grab.

clue.text: Labourer wants beer with lemonade essentially

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the outer letters of the drink are removed

parts.note: a shandy is beer mixed with lemonade

explanation.surface: A workman wants a shandy, essentially.
explanation.walkthrough: A shandy is a British pub drink of beer and lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm or factory worker is called a hand, as in farmhand or deckhand.

clue.text: Judge old King and Queen's jesters

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a queen, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A judge, an old king and the queen's court fools.
explanation.walkthrough: With the card-game theme, these are also the wild cards in a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesters are people who joke and play the fool, so the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Intrepid Sally on a fun helter-skelter

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the sally comes last
helter-skelter means in wild disorder, so the letters of a fun are jumbled

parts.note: a sally is a sudden attack or raid

explanation.surface: Fearless Sally rides a fairground helter-skelter for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: A helter-skelter is a British fairground spiral slide; here it signals the anagram UNAF of A FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and bold, a direct synonym of not being frightened.

clue.text: Stresses when grammar forms increase

parts.note: tenses are the verb forms of grammar such as past and present
to up is to increase

explanation.surface: Stress rises when grammatical forms multiply, as language learners know.
explanation.definitionFit: To get tense or tighten up under pressure is to be stressed, so the phrasal verb fits.

clue.text: Broker fermented red ale

indicators.note: fermenting churns and transforms its contents, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A trader sells home-brewed red ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker buys and sells for others, as a trader or merchant does.
